items.q: What quality most distinguishes a great negotiator in your experience?
items.a: It is patience above all — the discipline to wait when others would push — that distinguishes the closer who seals an agreement from the one who merely chases a transaction.

items.a: At the highest level, repetition signals carelessness, so a deal memo that moves between deal, transaction and agreement reads as the work of a considered mind.

items.a: What had begun as a guarded exchange had, by the closing call, ripened into a dialogue, and finally into something approaching a partnership.

items.a: It is restraint, not haste, that secures the better terms, and the deal lost to impatience is invariably more costly than the deal delayed by discipline.

items.a: The unspoken signals — a silence, a hesitation — often carry as much weight as the terms themselves, and reading them is the quiet art of the closer.
